host_pipeline.scope: host diagnostic only; not an edge-target measurement

camera_exposure.interpretation: The reported 1/64 s value is shorter than 1/30 s and does not explain the observed 7.5 FPS by exposure duration alone. This property read is not a sensor timestamp or proof of actual integration time.

runs.command: ffmpeg -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -pixel_format yuyv422 -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 60 -an -c:v copy -f rawvideo pipe:1
ffmpeg -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -vcodec mjpeg -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 60 -an -c:v copy -f image2pipe -vcodec copy pipe:1

runs.mode: libx264 Baseline/CAVLC to raw H.264, default output synchronization
runs.command: ffmpeg -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 20 -an -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -profile:v baseline -coder 0 -pix_fmt yuv420p -x264-params keyint=1:min-keyint=1:scenecut=0:repeat-headers=1 -g 1 -qp 22 -f h264 NUL

runs.mode: libx264 Baseline/CAVLC to raw H.264, fps_mode passthrough
runs.command: ffmpeg -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 20 -an -fps_mode passthrough -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -profile:v baseline -coder 0 -pix_fmt yuv420p -x264-params keyint=1:min-keyint=1:scenecut=0:repeat-headers=1 -g 1 -qp 22 -f h264 NUL

runs.mode: YUYV422 rawvideo passthrough at lowest advertised 30 FPS resolution; no encoder
runs.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -stats_period 1 -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -pixel_format yuyv422 -video_size 160x120 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 20 -an -fps_mode passthrough -f null NUL

runs.mode: MJPEG decode to null with default DirectShow device timestamps
runs.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -stats_period 1 -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 10 -an -fps_mode passthrough -f null NUL

runs.mode: MJPEG decode to null with wall-clock timestamps
runs.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -stats_period 1 -use_video_device_timestamps false -f dshow -rtbufsize 256K -video_size 352x288 -framerate 30 -i video=USB2.0 HD UVC WebCam -t 10 -an -fps_mode passthrough -f null NUL

interpretation: The camera advertises 30 FPS at 352x288 and 160x120, but independent raw YUYV and compressed MJPEG passthrough at 352x288 both yielded about 7.5 delivered frames/s in 60-second tests. A 20-second read-only raw YUYV test at 160x120 also produced 150 frames (7.5 FPS; FFmpeg speed 0.989x), so lowering spatial resolution alone did not restore the requested rate. Two sequential 10-second MJPEG decode-to-null sessions, one with default device timestamps and one using wall-clock timestamps, each delivered 75 frames (7.5 FPS; speed 0.975x); changing timestamp source did not restore frame delivery. The sessions were not simultaneous. Exposure query reports 1/64 s in auto; this is not an independent integration-time measurement. The matching low rate across raw and compressed output types and both tested resolutions indicates the bottleneck is before encoding and not explained by output synchronization; root cause within DirectShow delivery, device pacing, USB/host scheduling, or camera state remains unresolved. Raw-H.264 output with default synchronization emitted 600 frames in 20 seconds from 150 camera frames and FFmpeg reported 450 duplicates; setting -fps_mode passthrough emitted only the 150 source frames. The corrected 60-second full WebSocket/native E2E likewise emitted 450 frames at 7.608 FPS, with zero dropped chunks and all strict-decode/proof/key gates passing. Earlier 60-second/300-second E2E runs used default raw-H.264 synchronization, so their approximately 30-FPS output counts include synthetic duplicates and do not prove camera acquisition rate.
